chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Talaqani (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamdani narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal narrated to us from his father, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) say:

Indeed, I will be killed, poisoned, and buried in a strange land. I know this through a covenant that my father entrusted to me, from his father, from his forefathers, from the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family).

Surely, whoever visits me in my place of exile, my forefathers and I shall be his intercessors on the Day of Resurrection. And whoever has our intercession shall be saved, even if his sins were equivalent to the burden of the two heavyweights (humanity and the Jinn).

key_terms.الثقلين: The two heavyweights — refers to humanity (al-ins) and the Jinn, from Quran 55:31
key_terms.شفعاء: Intercessors — those who advocate on behalf of others before God on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.عهد: Covenant/testament — a sacred trust passed through the chain of Imams from the Prophet
key_terms.غربة: Estrangement/exile — refers to Khorasan, far from the Imam's homeland of Medina
key_terms.مسموم: Poisoned — indicates the method of his martyrdom by the Abbasid caliph al-Ma'mun

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Rida say about visiting his grave and intercession on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS), the eighth Imam, prophesies his own martyrdom by poisoning and burial in a foreign land (Tus/Mashhad in Khorasan, Iran). He states that this knowledge comes through a prophetic covenant passed down through the Imams from the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW). He then offers a tremendous reward for visiting his grave: the intercession of himself and all his forefathers (the Imams and the Prophet) on the Day of Judgment, which will save the visitor regardless of the weight of their sins. This hadith is historically significant as it was narrated before the Imam's actual martyrdom and has become one of the foundational texts for the practice of pilgrimage (ziyarah) to his shrine in Mashhad.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq al-Talaqani (ra) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Hamadani narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. al-Hasan b. `Ali b. Faddal narrated to us from his father. He said: I heard Aba’l Hasan `Ali b. Musa al-Rida (as) say:
Surely, I will be killed, poisoned, and buried in a strange land. I know that due to a covenant that was given to me by my father from his father from his forefathers from the Messenger of Allah (s).

Surely, he who visits me in my isolation shall have the intercession of my forefathers and I on the Day of Resurrection. He who has our intercession will be saved, even if his sins are like that of the two heavyweights (humanity and the Jinn).
